interceptors()

The interceptors() method registers interceptor behaviors on a FeatureCell that control when incoming state updates are allowed to enter the Vault pipeline. Interceptors execute before any resolution or transformation occurs and provide admission control without modifying state values.

Method Contract Summary

  • Interceptors execute before the Resolve stage
  • Interceptors never modify state values
  • Interceptors control timing, gating, or suppression of updates
  • Interceptors execute in initialization order
  • Errors propagate as Vault errors

The interceptors() method defines admission control only. It does not participate in state computation, resolution, merging, reduction, or snapshot emission. Its responsibility is limited to shaping the flow of incoming updates before pipeline execution begins.

Note

The interceptors() method is additive. It may be invoked multiple times, and each call appends interceptor behaviors to the FeatureCell’s interceptor list. Interceptors may be supplied as a single array or across multiple method invocations; in all cases, interceptors execute in the exact order they are registered during initialization.

While multiple invocations are supported, the recommended practice is to register related interceptor behaviors as a single ordered array to preserve clarity and intentional execution ordering.

Example

The interceptors() method registers one or more interceptor behaviors that execute before the Resolve stage of the pipeline. These behaviors observe raw incoming update requests and may delay, suppress, or gate execution without altering the value itself.

Example: Registering Interceptors

{{`employeeCell
  .interceptors([
    withDebounce(500),
    withThrottle(1000)
  ])
  .initialize();`}}

What this does

  • Registers interceptor behaviors on the FeatureCell
  • Interceptors execute before any state resolution
  • Incoming updates may be delayed, gated, or suppressed
  • No state values are modified or transformed

This demonstrates the intended use of interceptors() as a pre-processing mechanism for controlling update timing and admission into the pipeline.
